subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: For a manually configured iOS Remote Domain endpoint with a system-trusted hostname certificate, what stable identity should replace the current single-leaf fingerprint boundary?
rationale: Current pinning intentionally protects against gateway impersonation, but Cloudflare anycast makes a single mutable leaf fingerprint unusable; source inspection cannot choose the acceptable security tradeoff on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Split policy by connection mode
options.body: Use platform CA and hostname validation for public Remote Domain endpoints while retaining TOFU leaf pinning for discovered or self-signed gateways and binding paired sessions to gateway authentication identity.

options.title: Support multiple scoped pins
options.body: Persist a bounded set of trusted leaf fingerprints per gateway, accepting operational complexity and continued churn whenever Cloudflare introduces an unseen certificate.

options.title: Retain strict single-leaf pinning
options.body: Keep the present security model and document Cloudflare anycast TLS termination as unsupported for Remote Domain connections.

recommendation.title: Split policy by connection mode
recommendation.body: Use platform CA and hostname validation for public Remote Domain endpoints while retaining TOFU leaf pinning for discovered or self-signed gateways and binding paired sessions to gateway authentication identity.

likelyOwner.reason: The ownership documentation and recent history connect this person to both the iOS app and its security-sensitive connection flow.
